purpose: Candesartan is used to treat high blood pressure, which helps lower your risk of heart attacks, strokes, and kidney problems. It is also used in adults and some children to treat heart failure, a condition where the heart does not pump blood as well as it should. Keeping your blood pressure under control is very important for your overall health.
how_it_works: Your body makes a chemical called angiotensin II that causes your blood vessels to tighten and squeeze, which raises your blood pressure. Candesartan blocks the receptors that this chemical attaches to, so your blood vessels stay relaxed and open. This makes it easier for your heart to pump blood and brings your blood pressure down to a healthier level.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include dizziness, especially when standing up quickly, headache, back pain, and a runny or stuffy nose. Some people may feel tired or notice mild flu-like symptoms. These effects are usually mild and often improve as your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Do not take candesartan if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can seriously harm or even cause the death of an unborn baby. Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, or if you are taking potassium supplements, since this medicine can raise potassium levels in your blood. Avoid using salt substitutes that contain potassium, and do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: For high blood pressure, the usual starting dose is 8 mg once a day, and your doctor may increase it up to 32 mg once daily depending on how your body responds. For heart failure, dosing often starts low and is gradually increased. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes, with or without food, at the same time each day.
